role.altitude: The emergency management director keeps planning with partners, training groups, advising communities, comparing plans and signing off funding; copying figures, chasing partners, rebuilding templates and checklists and copying measures shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping template and plan libraries current
role.ambitious_version: A director who helps more small communities because templates and answers are ready.

tasks.short: Read the call, plan with partners and finance, write the application, build the budget, enter, check and submit the application for federal funding, track grant spending, collect partner figures, write, check and submit progress reports, check grant status and coordinate with the funder to administer and report on the progress of grants.

steps.what: Director reads the funding call and eligibility rules
Director plans the application with partners and finance
Director writes the application narrative

loop.input: Earlier applications, the plan and the director's notes.
loop.check: Every claim and figure must trace to the plan, the budget or a logged fact, and every source cited must resolve; the director rewrites the argument.
loop.stop: The director writes the section when two drafts cite something that does not resolve.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each call asks for a different case.

steps.what: Director builds the budget in a spreadsheet, typing cost rates from finance reports
Director enters the application in the grant portal
Director checks the final application and signs it off
Director submits the approved application for federal funding
Director copies grant expenditures from finance reports into the grant spreadsheet
Director chases partners for their progress figures by mail
Partner enters progress figures in the shared reporting form
Director writes the progress report on the grant

loop.input: Earlier applications, the plan and the director's notes.
loop.check: Every claim and figure must trace to the plan, the budget or a logged fact, and every source cited must resolve; the director rewrites the argument.
loop.stop: The director writes the section when two drafts cite something that does not resolve.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each call asks for a different case.

steps.what: Director enters progress data in the grant portal
Director checks the final progress report and portal entries
Director submits the approved progress report to the funder
Director checks grant status and payments in the portal
Director answers funder questions and coordinates partners by mail
Director meets the funder and partners on progress

approvals.approved_version: The application text, budget and portal entries exactly as checked and signed off by the director in s6, submitted to the funder named in the call; any change needs a new sign-off.
The progress report and portal entries for that reporting period exactly as checked by the director in s13, submitted to the same funder; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The application and progress narratives start from drafts based on earlier applications, the plan and logged facts; every claim must trace to a source that resolves, and the director rewrites the argument. The budget template reads cost rates from the finance export. Expenditures coded to the grant in the finance system feed the spending table, instead of copying them. Partners enter their figures in a shared form with deadline reminders, instead of being chased by mail. Planning, portal entry, sign-offs, submissions, status checks, funder contact and meetings stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were copied from finance and partners chased by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Grant cost codes in the finance system, shared reporting forms and drafting tied to sources.
tasks.still_hard: Calls with new formats each year.
tasks.human_edge: Making the case for funding a risk that has not happened yet.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and chasing; the funding case stays.

evidence.claim: Budgets and reports are generated from the ERP without Excel rekeying; a model drafts commentary checked against the figures.
A review partly drafted with a language model cited non-existent sources and a fabricated court case, and the firm agreed to repay.

assumptions: Boundary: applying for and administering grants; helping communities apply (task 7275) is in this set and a separate task.
Input contract for s8: grant expenditures carry the grant cost code in the finance system; s8 is priced at that.
s3 is priced at 85 and s11 at 75 because the director rewrites the argument; s4 saves typing rates; s9 keeps 40 for late partners.
Partners' form time is shown in s10 and replaces their mailed figures.
research_questions: Are progress reports submitted on time more often?

incremental.description: Director keeps the reporting form current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one small grant; high: several grants with many partners.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange sessions, let groups register, prepare training materials, keep the plan-requirement checklist, run workshops, coach groups, review their draft plans, answer questions, keep attendance and share materials to train local groups in the preparation of long-term plans compatible with federal and state plans.

steps.what: Director arranges training sessions and registrations by mail
Group member registers for a session on the registration form
Director rebuilds the checklist of plan elements required by federal and state plans
Director prepares training materials

loop.input: The director's outline, the requirement checklist and earlier materials.
loop.check: The director checks every requirement against the federal and state plan text.
loop.stop: The director writes the material when two drafts misstate a requirement.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each group and plan cycle needs its own examples.

steps.what: Director trains local groups in the preparation of long-term plans in workshops
Director coaches groups one to one on their plans
Director reviews groups' draft plans against the requirements
Director answers group questions by mail
Director keeps attendance in a spreadsheet
Director uploads materials to the shared portal

tasks.design: Group members register on a form that keeps the attendance list, instead of arranging sessions by mail and keeping a spreadsheet. The checklist of required plan elements is kept in the plan library with review dates and reused, instead of being rebuilt each time. Training materials start from drafts checked against the plan text. Workshops, coaching, reviewing draft plans, questions and sharing materials stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sessions, attendance and requirement lists were rebuilt by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Registration forms and a plan library with review dates.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a volunteer group see which risks matter most locally.

evidence.claim: A plan library with test and review dates is a records app.

assumptions: Boundary: training local groups on plans; reviewing organisations' emergency plans (task 7269) and designing preparedness courses (task 7261) are sibling tasks.
s1 keeps 40 for sessions arranged by phone; s3 keeps 50 for updates when plans change; s4 is priced at 90; s9 keeps 40 for walk-ins.
Group members' registration time is shown in s2.
unknowns: Number of groups trained per year.
research_questions: Do group plans meet the requirements more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few groups; high: many groups each cycle.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read call documents, meet community officials, run application workshops, discuss calls with communities, answer eligibility questions, write templates and guidance, compile cost tables, check application completeness, review drafts, look up eligibility and help enter applications to assist communities in applying for federal funding.

steps.what: Director reads call documents and rules
Director meets community officials to scope their needs
Director discusses upcoming calls with communities by mail
Director writes application templates and guidance for communities
Director runs application workshops for communities
Director answers communities' eligibility questions by mail
Director compiles cost tables for facilities and radiological instrumentation from price lists
Director looks up eligibility and application status in the funding portal
Director reviews communities' draft applications and comments
Director checks applications for completeness against the call checklist
Director helps communities enter applications in the portal

tasks.design: A template library holds application sections and guidance per call type, and the director updates it per call instead of rewriting. A page with an eligibility checklist and answers to common questions lets one answer reach every community. A shared price list with formulas builds cost tables, instead of typing prices per application. A completeness checklist with rules flags missing parts. Reading calls, meetings, workshops, reviewing drafts, portal look-ups and helping with entry stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates, answers and cost tables were rebuilt for each community.
tasks.enabler_now: Template libraries, question pages, shared price lists and completeness rules.
tasks.still_hard: Small communities with no grant experience.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which community need a funder will recognise.

ambition.what: Help small communities that never applied because the effort was too high.

tasks.altitude: Less rewriting and typing; advice stays.

reach.learn: Whether applications are complete the first time.

evidence.claim: Records apps with notifications replace registers and mail-outs in Excel, Word and Outlook.

assumptions: Boundary: assisting communities with applications; applying for own grants (task 7272) is in this set and a separate task.
s4 and s6 keep 70; s7 keeps 60 for items not on the price list; s10 keeps 50 for judgement on unclear parts.
Reading, meetings, workshops, reviews, look-ups and portal help keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of communities assisted per call.
research_questions: Are fewer applications returned as incomplete?

incremental.description: Director keeps the template library and price list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one community; high: many communities per call.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search for and request emergency plans used elsewhere, read and compare them, extract key measures, copy them into a comparison sheet, write a lessons summary, discuss with colleagues in other regions and by mail to gather information for plan development.

steps.what: Director searches for emergency plans used elsewhere
Director requests plans from other agencies by mail
Director reads and compares the plans
Director notes key measures from each plan

loop.output: Key measures per plan with page references in a table.
loop.check: The director checks every extracted measure against its page.
loop.stop: The director notes measures by hand when a plan is a scan with no text.
loop.why_not_simpler: Plans describe measures in different structures.

steps.what: Director copies measures from the notes into the comparison spreadsheet
Director discusses plans with colleagues in other regions
Director discusses plans with colleagues by mail
Director writes the lessons summary for plan development

tasks.design: A shared plan library among regions with saved searches replaces searching for each plan. An extraction step lists key measures per plan with page references, the director checks each against its page, and the table feeds the comparison sheet, instead of copying notes into it. Requesting plans, reading and comparing, discussions and the lessons summary stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were searched for and measures copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared plan libraries and extraction with page references.
tasks.still_hard: Plans kept confidential by other agencies.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a measure that worked elsewhere will fail here.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and copying; comparison stays.

evidence.claim: A model summarises documents and proposes affected policies; an owner decides.
A review partly drafted with a language model cited non-existent sources, so every measure needs a page reference.

assumptions: Boundary: studying plans used elsewhere; preparing own plans (task 7254) and keeping plans compliant with regulations (task 7259) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: about half of relevant plans are in the shared library; s1 is priced at that share.
s4 is priced at 70 because every measure is checked; s5 saves copying.
Requests, reading, discussions and the summary keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of plans reviewed per cycle.
research_questions: Are more plans compared per cycle?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few plans; high: many plans in the shared library.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
